title: test-0046-SCI-BIO-MOVEMENT
passage: Many people mistakenly believe that our skeleton is just a rigid, solid frame like a statue, but this is far from the truth. Your backbone is not one single, long, continuous bone; instead, it is made of many small, individual vertebrae stacked together, which allows your body to bend and twist. Similarly, the rib cage is not a solid wall of bone, but a flexible structure that expands and contracts as you breathe. You might also think that all joints are designed for movement, but some, like those in your skull, are fixed and do not move at all. Furthermore, bones are not dead, non-living structures like rocks. They are living tissues that grow, repair themselves, and contain blood vessels. Between many of our bones, we find cartilage, which is a flexible, smooth tissue. It is not just 'soft bone' waiting to harden; it serves a permanent purpose by reducing friction and cushioning joints throughout our entire lives. Finally, remember that muscles are not just for lifting heavy weights in your arms or legs. They are found throughout your body, including your internal organs, and they work in pairs to move bones by pulling, never by pushing.
summary: The rib cage is not a solid wall of bones, but a flexible structure that changes shape when you breathe. They are found throughout your body, including your internal organs, and they work in pairs to move bones by pulling, never by pushing.
